test: unassigned counters and unknown targets report actionable errors
reason: Invalid XP references, a Level not assigned to the player and an unknown profile target must identify the corresponding unresolved names/catalogs in allocatePlan errors. These diagnostics let a failed plan be repaired instead of silently binding to the wrong actor fields.

test: planner repairs invalid counter names without changing allocated shared fields
reason: Starts generation with an invalid planned XP name, verifies a second planning request includes repair errors, and checks the accepted catalog contains only one XP field. This catches repair orchestration that duplicates/reallocates fields after a planning correction.

test: generation requests and validates canonical XP defaults and managed levels
reason: Checks the actual stats request carries canonical XP defaults and unlocked XP/managed Level requirements for both enabled owners, then validates the resulting definition and rejects a non-remainder XP default. Added explicit owner coverage so an empty counterRequirements array cannot satisfy the loop.

test: System generation forwards Additional Parameters from its captured connection preset
reason: Exercises the generation adapter with a captured Custom profile preset and checks Additional Parameters/header macro values and a live cancellation signal reach sendRequest. The profile helper alone cannot detect dropping its payload in this caller.

test: selected profile receives schema, budget, signal and dedicated prompts; preferences are captured
reason: Mutates tracker preferences after adapter creation and verifies the captured profile, schema toggle, token budget, temperature and usage kind are used. Added an assertion for the forwarded system/user messages because the existing title claimed dedicated-prompt forwarding without testing it.

test: profile failures never switch to main API and aborted requests never dispatch
reason: A selected-profile error must propagate without a main-API call, and a pre-aborted signal must not send another selected request. This protects deliberate connection choice and avoids spending tokens after cancellation.

test: main API supports both structured and ordinary text paths
reason: Exercises separate main-API structured and ordinary response paths: raw provider text is extracted only without schema mode, while schema objects and the schema argument are preserved in structured mode.

test: NPC creation uses its explicit lore connection and separate usage counter
reason: Explicit lore profile and NPC usage arguments override tracker reader defaults in the shared adapter. This prevents NPC creation from using the wrong model/usage bucket even when System-generation defaults work.

test: Stop cancels main API System/NPC generation and ignores late responses
reason: For the main API path, Stop must reject promptly, abort the forwarded signal, ignore a late provider response, record no usage and release listeners/button state. Main and profile paths forward their signals through different host calls.

test: Stop cancels profile System/NPC generation and ignores late responses
reason: For the selected-profile path, Stop must reject promptly, abort the sendRequest signal, ignore a late profile response, record no usage and release listeners/button state. This separately verifies the profile host boundary.

test: staged generation assembles canonical System with template progression and typed rewards
reason: Runs the complete staged generator and checks validated output, typed reward entries, actor targets, progression, primary-field display defaults and usage accounting. This is the main successful assembly integration, not a copy of any one validator test.

test: malformed shared catalog repairs once; retry preserves accepted work
reason: Truncates the shared-stat response until generation fails, retries the same run, and checks already accepted world stats were requested only once and preserved. It prevents costly replay or replacement of completed sections on retry.

test: progression growth candidates cannot include counters
reason: Injects Level as a growth candidate in a generated catalog; the stage must fail without enabling NPC progression. Schema/semantic acceptance here could let automatic growth change its own level counter.

test: NPC catalog requests pin shared IDs and repair invented archetype suffixes
reason: Corrupts planned IDs and checks a repair is requested with independently narrowed schema enums for each owner; collections/rewards receive selected dependencies, and final catalogs/HUD IDs agree. This guards ID/reference corruption during staged generation.

test: invalid XP is repaired with its stats, before progression or dependents are accepted
reason: Invalid plain XP/default capacity must fail the stat stage, leave its catalog and progression unaccepted, and prevent dependent collection requests; retry must preserve accepted profile work. It protects atomic stage acceptance and runnable generated progression.

test: generation assembles multiple templates and collections
reason: Generates two templates and two collections with different progression/reward choices and validates the combined definition. Single-template happy-path assembly cannot catch owner/collection collapsing in a multi-owner plan.

test: cancellation returns promptly, prevents dependent requests and ignores late response
reason: Aborts while a world-stat promise is pending and verifies prompt rejection, no late acceptance, no following requests and an incomplete run. This catches orchestrator-level cancellation beyond request-adapter Stop tests.

test: ambiguous plans reject references before defining catalogs; IDs deterministic and frozen
renamed_to: ambiguous plans reject references before defining catalogs and IDs remain deterministic
reason: Checks ambiguous case-insensitive names reject and renamed XP references resolve to a stable slug; repeated allocation stays deterministic. Removed Object.isFrozen assertion because immutability mechanism is an implementation choice, while stable allocated identity matters.

test: strict validation rejects semantic corruption before normalization can repair it
reason: Mutates valid generated definitions across numeric defaults, bounds, targets, counter ownership, reward fields, HUD references, markup and forbidden data. Every corruption must produce errors and no finalized definition, preventing normalization from silently accepting unsafe/inconsistent rules.

test: draft projection is isolated; errors stay visible rather than normalized away
reason: Edits an isolated draft projection and saves it; the original stays unchanged, the changed name reaches the captured draft, and an invalid minimum remains visible to validation instead of being normalized away. This protects live settings while users review generated rules.

test: draft may retain reusable fields after their sole template is removed
reason: Removes the only template from an editable draft and its assignments, then captures a valid definition retaining an unassigned reusable profile field. It guards legitimate Builder editing from deleting reusable definitions or retaining dangling actor references.

test: catalog stage cannot silently change planned field assignments
reason: Returns a profile with targets changed from the allocated plan and requires the profiles stage to fail. This catches a model response that broadens field ownership despite otherwise well-shaped data.

test: legacy same-named definitions remain valid when actor assignments are disjoint
reason: Creates same-named player and NPC XP/profile definitions with disjoint targets and verifies validity/finalization, then broadens NPC XP to overlap the player and requires a duplicate error. It protects independent actor schemas imported from legacy data.

test: legacy template named player retains NPC-specific counter assignments
reason: Uses a legacy NPC template literally named player with player progression disabled and template-qualified assignments; validation must retain NPC-specific progression instead of confusing that identifier with the player owner.

test: response parser rejects truncation and handles prose/fences
reason: Checks the strict generation parser accepts a fenced object but rejects incomplete JSON and arrays. Permissive reader repair is intentionally a different contract; generated reusable rules must not be fabricated from truncation.

test: minimal System needs only planning; guided rewards and independent NPC policies work
reason: A plan with no fields/templates/collections must complete without requesting nonexistent stages; a separate guided reward case preserves disabled player progression while NPC progression remains enabled. It covers optional stage graphs and independent owner policies.

test: request limits, excess object counts, unknown section data, and network failures are bounded
reason: Excess templates and the request budget must reject, a network exception must dispatch only once, and unrequested top-level section data must fail. These bounds prevent runaway generation and accidental acceptance of mixed responses.

test: saved fixture drives normal progression, bounded growth, and scheduled target rewards
reason: Loads a frozen generated fixture and independently invokes XP, stat boost and reward primitives with hardcoded expected arithmetic. Full fixture import/capture validation already exists and dedicated progression/reward tests exercise these same operations, so this extra synthetic integration adds no distinct boundary.
covered_by: tests/system-preset-migration.mjs: generated fixture imports without activation and retains rules through capture/export; tests/progression.mjs; tests/collection-rewards.mjs

test: generation preserves and validates planned memory rules
reason: Checks planned memory settings reach stage context and final output, then rejects invalid enable/carryover flags, missing carryover, interval/cap/guidance limits and legacy profile policies. This verifies strict generated-rule validation, unlike forgiving import normalization.

test: generated Systems preserve place discovery opt-out and validate its configuration
reason: Generates a plan explicitly disabling Places and verifies that setting reaches subsequent requests and the final definition; missing, mistyped or world-data-bearing location rules cannot finalize. This prevents opt-out loss and story state leaking into reusable rules.

test: renaming preserves chat/roster ownership, canonical ID, capture and restoration
reason: Renames a System display name/description while its library key, canonical ID, chat reference and roster ownership remain stable; capture, export/import and restoration preserve it. Relaxed the exact duplicate-import suffix, retaining distinct-name behavior.

test: invalid names cannot overwrite a saved key or another display name
reason: Blank and colliding names cannot rename/create a System or overwrite another saved key, and refused operations do not save. This prevents destructive library collisions beyond simple cosmetic name formatting.

test: active duplication captures current controls and independently copies NPCs, Places and memories
reason: Duplicates the active System after unsaved HUD changes and deeply mutates copied cards, places, memories and rules to prove the source remains independent and the active chat owner stays unchanged. Removed the exact copy-name suffix while retaining uniqueness across repeated copies.

test: inactive duplication retains its own settings and supports Places carryover alone
reason: Duplicates an inactive System while live controls belong elsewhere; copied rules/config must come from the inactive source, Place-only reuse remains independent, and the source/active selection stay unchanged. This is distinct from capturing active controls.

test: chat ownership remains default; enabling publishes only portable values
reason: Roster reuse remains opt-in; enabling captures carryover stats and portable identity fields but excludes per-adventure HP/items/memories; protects the fork’s chat-owned default.

test: new chats get independent copies once; defaults reset and deletions stay local
reason: New chats receive independent IDs/profiles, reset variable stats/inventory, seed only once, and cannot publish a local deletion as roster deletion; protects reusable source cards from shared references and accidental erasure.

test: older unchanged copies do not undo roster edits; changed copies publish for future chats
reason: Changed copies publish renamed/profile/stat values for future chats, but reopening an older unchanged copy cannot overwrite the newer roster source; exercises optimistic publication signatures.

test: reused renamed NPCs retain their gallery folder and independent portrait tags
reason: Renamed NPCs retain their original image folder and gallery/tag data through capture and seeding, while edits on either original or seeded tags do not mutate the saved roster; protects media ownership.

test: rosters respect System, started chat, disabled mode and closed chat boundaries
reason: Roster capture/seeding respects the selected System, started-chat gate, disabled reuse and absent open chat; prevents copying NPCs into another adventure or retroactively populating a played chat.

test: invalid imported roster shapes are repaired
reason: Imported null/malformed roster records and invalid card entries normalize safely with strict boolean options; prevents crashes or accidental opt-in after importing bad settings.

test: the old Manager memory option migrates once into canonical System rules
reason: Old reuseMemories migrates into canonical carryOver once without losing saved memories or overriding an explicit later choice; protects existing user data during the settings transition.

test: choosing another System before play replaces only automatically seeded cards
reason: Changing System before play removes only automatically seeded prior-System cards, retains manually created chat cards, and can seed the first System again; protects deliberate local content during setup changes.

test: template field assignments govern carryover and clearing does not republish unchanged copies
reason: Canonical template assignments select only opted-in stat readings and preserve cleared rosters against unchanged source/copied cards and transient empty projections; prevents stale roster resurrection or stat stripping.

test: portrait cleanup protects saved rosters even when reuse is disabled
reason: Image-reference cleanup includes all portraits of saved roster cards even while reuse is disabled; prevents cleanup deleting media for a preserved reusable roster.

test: a fresh install adopts an editable Fantasy Adventure System
reason: Builds fresh-install settings and runs adoption to ensure the seeded editable starter becomes active, the chat binding callback runs once and shipped defaults stay unmodified. It catches new-install activation/wiring failures not exercised by factory validation alone.

test: System switches and creation preserve the user menu text size
reason: Applies, captures and creates Systems while a user font scale differs from the imported scale; the user preference must survive and stay out of captured System config. This checks settings ownership, not a particular font size/design.

test: loaded legacy world is discarded and stays outside the System
reason: Migrates a saved preset containing legacy embedded world/character/persona data and verifies applying/capturing it cannot replace live characters or include those records in reusable definitions. This protects chat data at startup migration.

test: old profile import ignores its world; modern definition import is usable
reason: Imports old and modern rule shapes, excludes embedded story data, avoids name collisions and checks a started chat cannot switch/create Systems while an unplayed chat can rebind/reset. This integration exercises import and chat-lock boundaries, though the shared fixture makes cases order-dependent.

test: template definitions survive System capture and modern import
reason: Imports/captures a legacy template definition and verifies memberships survive; creating a new empty System must not inherit the previous template or legacy assignment marker. This guards rule reuse and clean creation independently of runtime actor selection.

test: canonical progression projects into live tracker and survives capture
reason: Applies migrated rules with separately named player/NPC counters, then captures them; runtime tracker IDs and enabled NPC progression must project from canonical rules and survive saving.

test: generated fixture imports without activation and retains rules through capture/export
reason: Imports the saved generated fixture without activation and verifies only the library changes, then applies/captures it and compares HUD, progression, templates, collections, stats and memories. This is the saved generated-rule round-trip boundary used instead of redundant fixture arithmetic.

test: capture preserves canonical edits and omits runtime projection catalogs
reason: Changes canonical stat text while a tracker projection is stale and saves; canonical edits must win, and projected catalog/progression/location keys must be stripped from saved config. Otherwise future loads can overwrite edited rules with stale copies.

test: capture retains collection and HUD edits made through tracker controls
reason: Edits collection name/targets/guidance and HUD toggles through tracker controls, then captures; those edits must persist while canonical stats and selected HUD field IDs remain intact. These controls still use projections, unlike canonical stat editors.

test: starter import resets System-owned settings and activates without changing saved story data
reason: Imports and activates a shipped starter over a live configuration: rule-owned defaults reset but current characters/persona data and pre-activation selection remain intact. It catches improper root-setting copying from starter payloads.

test: existing schema-2 presets acquire System-owned places and retain canonical toggles through capture
reason: Migrates a schema-2 preset missing Places rules, then changes the canonical toggle, captures and reapplies it. The toggle must survive without duplicated projected config, preventing a current-schema migration fast path from dropping newer rules.

test: local NPC rosters stay outside captured and imported rules and are removed with their System
reason: Captures/imports Systems containing local roster data and requires that data stay out of reusable rule config; applying another System preserves the existing roster, while deleting its owner removes it. This protects ownership and export privacy.

test: generated profiles preserve explicit badge and text-section choices
reason: Generated profile responses explicitly choose badge versus text-section booleans; those choices must survive assembly, and a missing choice must fail validation. This preserves configurable field metadata rather than a shipped visual arrangement.

test: generation repairs an omitted display choice before accepting profile fields
reason: Deletes a required profile display choice from the first stage response and checks repair errors prompt a second response before a valid definition is accepted. This exercises a required-field repair path using real profile data.

test: reordering inserts before or after a destination in either direction
reason: Moves list objects before/after targets in both index directions and verifies exact resulting order. Off-by-one destination errors directly corrupt user-requested field ordering.

test: protected prefixes, foreign objects, and unchanged positions do not mutate the list
reason: Rejects protected identifier moves, foreign objects and no-op destinations without mutating the list, then permits insertion just after the protected prefix. This guards pinned collection identity and list integrity during reordering.

test: Places and NPC memories are excluded by default, independently of NPC reuse
reason: Enabling NPC reuse alone does not copy Places or NPC memories into a fresh chat or allocate them in the saved roster; preserves independently opted-in adventure-state reuse.

test: Places copy their graph and lore references independently while the current place resets
reason: Copied Places retain parent graph, aliases and lore-entry references, reset the current location, and are independent until explicit publication; protects reusable maps from accidental linkage.

test: copied active and archived memories use the fresh NPC identity and survive old-source invalidation
reason: Copied active/archive memories are keyed to the new NPC ID, lose old reply provenance, survive invalidation, exclude player memories and remain independent until republished; protects portable knowledge from old-chat deletion.

test: Places work without NPC reuse; memory reuse requires NPC reuse and honors both opt-outs
reason: Places reuse can operate without NPC reuse, each option can be turned off, and memories require their own carryOver rule; checks independent option gates rather than cosmetic defaults.

test: unchanged older chats cannot overwrite newer map or memory edits
reason: Publishing newer map and memory edits then revisiting an older unchanged chat cannot roll back either saved source; protects source freshness for non-card roster state.

test: started chats and user-created maps remain intact, and seeding never repeats
reason: Played chats never receive an initial roster seed, emptied maps are not repopulated on repeat seeding, and existing user-authored maps take precedence; protects active adventures and deliberate deletions.

test: System changes before play remove only seeded Places and NPC memories
reason: Before-play System switching removes only seeded map/memory entries, repairs a retained local place’s removed parent link, and leaves manually created knowledge intact; protects selective cleanup and graph validity.

test: clear saved roster clears map and memories without republishing unchanged chat state
reason: Clearing saved roster state does not immediately resurrect the old map or memories from an unchanged chat; prevents the clear action being silently undone by routine capture.

test: tracker-only saves publish Places and memory edits through the production storage boundary
reason: Actual tracker storage saves publish changed Places/memories into the matching System roster and stop publishing after a System mismatch; catches integration wiring absent from pure capture function tests.

test: legacy preset migration keeps only reusable schema and stable generated IDs
reason: Normalizes a legacy profile into stable field IDs/progression/hints while excluding character/world/master-item state and verifies the canonical result is idempotent. It protects old export readability and reusable-rule isolation.

test: System definitions retain collection image prompt choices
reason: An explicit collection image-prompt exclusion must survive normalization and another round trip. Losing this flag can unexpectedly include hidden belongings in generated portraits.

test: player and NPC profiles differ and label edits preserve field IDs
reason: Default player/NPC profile selection differs and renaming an NPC field label keeps its immutable ID and edited label on another normalization pass. This protects saved value lookup when users edit labels.

test: modern definitions bound memory limits and retain configured fields
reason: Keeps explicitly configured player/NPC profile fields and an intentionally empty player stat list when reading schema-1 data, while an out-of-range memory cap falls back to a valid value. The other memory case exercises valid caps/intervals but does not replace this invalid-cap branch.

test: stat purpose and numeric bounds survive system normalization
reason: Legacy numeric fields retain purpose, min/max and locked flags through normalization while incompatible text options are removed; the normalized result must be stable. This protects playable stat behavior and user-authored guidance in imported rules.

test: duplicate legacy names receive distinct IDs without mutating input
reason: Two legacy names that slug to the same ID must receive distinct stable IDs and the caller input must not mutate. Without this, an import can merge/overwrite unrelated saved field values.

test: System memory capture is opt-in, independently configured, and bounded
reason: Valid explicit memory rules round-trip; malformed intervals, booleans and excessive guidance are repaired, and carryover remains independent of auto-reading. The exact default values form import fallback behavior, unlike prose/style snapshots.

test: retired HUD layouts resolve to a supported style
reason: Asserts four retired HUD design names map to exact surviving visual styles across helpers/normalization. Those historical aesthetic correspondences are not consequential data/functionality contracts and constrain harmless fallback redesigns.

test: shared catalogs merge equivalent definitions and remap independent legacy references
reason: Merges equivalent legacy player/NPC definitions but keeps different XP capacities separate, remaps progression/HUD references and preserves the legacy profile value ID. This catches destructive catalog consolidation and dangling references on import.

test: stat display normalization keeps only show-name and value-only formats
reason: Normalizes unsupported legacy stat display templates into supported show-name/value-only formats and verifies idempotence. This guards unsupported markup/template tokens entering the runtime formatter rather than freezing a UI label.

test: shared assignments apply to player, every NPC, or a specific template
reason: Shared field targets distinguish player, all NPCs and a specific template, including the no-actor catalog query; NPC profile selection follows the same assignment vocabulary. This prevents actor-specific fields being exposed or updated on the wrong owner.

test: places default on for existing Systems and preserve explicit opt-out without world data
reason: Missing Places settings across old shapes adopt a usable default; explicit opt-outs survive while saved map records are excluded, and mutating the runtime projection cannot change canonical rules. This protects migration, rule/state isolation and copying.

test: import repair rejects CSS injection and malformed overrides, retaining zero and transparency
reason: Feeds malformed override objects, unknown options/keys, CSS injection, numeric strings and out-of-range values through normalization; invalid input is discarded while transparent color and numeric zero survive idempotently. This covers the imported-data/CSS boundary.

test: switching presets and resetting remove stale inline effects without changing component classes
reason: Applies overrides then switches/resets presets, checking user values and zero controls reach CSS/attributes and stale effects disappear without removing component classes. Relaxed exact compact-spacing pixels and the spelling of a transparent shadow to avoid cosmetic implementation locks.

test: the tracker stays on visible prose after generated images
reason: Checks generated image-only messages are classified and skipped as anchors until newer visible prose arrives; prevents tracker being hidden with host image text containers.

test: ordinary media and an empty chat keep their expected anchors
reason: Checks empty chat, ordinary single prose, inline-image message and only noninline image choose correct anchors; distinct empty/no-visible-anchor and host media modes.

test: model blank numeric readings preserve held ratings and pools in every scope
reason: Asserts blank/null numeric model readings are omitted with diagnostics across scopes, pool/rating types and flat shapes; prevents empty output erasing saved numeric state.

test: zero, text clearing, and manual numeric clearing keep their existing meaning
reason: Asserts explicit numeric zero and text clearing are permitted while whole-value manual numeric clearing remains valid; prevents blank-input protection from blocking legitimate edits.

test: a blank model pool initialization is omitted rather than becoming a bogus maximum
reason: Asserts a blank fresh-NPC pool value is omitted with one diagnostic instead of creating an invalid capacity; protects new actor initialization rather than just existing numeric state.

test: production dry run preserves held relationship stats after a blank model reply
reason: Asserts actual production dry-run application preserves all held relationship ratings after blank model output, with diagnostics; verifies the sanitizer-to-application boundary beyond primitive rejection.

test: unnamed collections use the single collection applicable to each actor
reason: Normalizes omitted collection IDs into the only applicable player/NPC collection without warnings. Protects model output recovery while retaining actor targets.

test: ambiguous collections are skipped with a visible explanation; named ones stay intact
reason: Skips ambiguous unnamed collection operations with a diagnostic and preserves already-named payloads. Protects against guessing the wrong inventory.

test: overlapping automatic turns read in order using the preceding applied state
reason: Runs two automatic readings concurrently through the production queue/extraction wrapper; verifies second prompt uses first applied XP, requests remain ordered, and final state reflects second turn.

test: Stop cancels both the active reading and a waiting turn without starting its request
reason: Stops one active and one waiting production extraction; verifies both cancel, waiting request never starts and held XP remains. Integration checks queue wiring to extraction.

test: reader reports skipped collection proposals even with no review rows and clears them on regeneration
reason: Checks collection refusal diagnostics are saved even with no pending diff and are replaced by clean regeneration. Retained for troubleshooting rejected model changes, not exact prose.

test: regeneration replaces XP and applied rows, clears old proposals and keeps manual edits
reason: Regenerates from pre-turn XP while retaining a later HP correction, clears old pending/applied records and repeats regeneration without stacking changes. Protects replacement orchestration.

test: an unusable regeneration leaves the previous reading and pending proposals intact
reason: Returns an unusable regeneration response and verifies prior XP, review proposals, and applied records all survive. Protects failure rollback.

test: a new turn arriving during regeneration prevents replacing the older turn
reason: Adds a newer turn while regeneration request runs and verifies the older turn cannot be replaced. Protects latest-turn ownership after asynchronous work.

test: manual changes during the request survive replacement
reason: Edits live HP while regeneration request waits and verifies the manual correction survives alongside regenerated XP. Distinct in-flight merge case.

test: manual mode skips automatic requests and replaces an explicitly requested reading
reason: In manual mode, automatic requests are skipped while explicit manual regeneration works repeatedly without stacked applied rows. Protects opt-in dispatch and replacement.

test: manual reading is discarded if a new turn arrives during the request
reason: In manual mode, adds a newer turn during a request and verifies the result is refused and old XP stays. Covers manual freshness independent of regeneration.

test: manual mode does not enable the reader in inline mode
reason: Passes manual:true in inline mode and verifies it cannot activate the separate reader. Prevents combining mutually exclusive reading modes.

test: master switch blocks forced reads and discards replies from an in-flight read
reason: Disables the master switch before force and during a live request; verifies no prompt starts or stale result commits and prior pending state remains.

test: stat rejection warnings persist without review rows and regeneration removes stale warnings
reason: Runs a real numeric normalization rejection with no diff; checks original output and diagnostics remain available, then clean regeneration removes old warnings. Distinct from collection warnings because source is normalization.

test: Stop preserves the previous reading and permits a clean retry
reason: Stops regeneration before commit and checks unchanged state/proposals, cancelled report and listener cleanup, then verifies a new attempt succeeds. Protects cancellation rollback and retry.

test: a new swipe retaining outgoing prose restores the narrator base before generation
reason: Creates a new host swipe slot while old prose/extra remain, preserves a later manual HP correction, clears only incoming turn data, and returns to the saved old swipe restoring its XP/profile. Protects host lifecycle integration.

test: an existing swipe restores its saved effects
reason: Loads an already saved alternate swipe and verifies its own XP/HP effects replace the outgoing state without warning. Covers valid-effect replay versus absent new slots.

test: changed text in a saved swipe still warns instead of replaying stale effects
reason: Edits text under a saved swipe and verifies stale effects are retained but not replayed, with a visible warning. Protects against mismatched source replay.

test: an empty incoming slot also restores the pre-reply state
reason: Clears incoming prose without creating a new slot and verifies pre-reply state is restored. Covers the separate empty-slot detection branch in onSwipe.

test: commits real newline boundaries and flushes the final unfinished line once
reason: The raw line parser must wait for actual newline boundaries, expose correct source ranges and flush an unfinished tail only once at finalization; repeated final pushes cannot replay it.

test: repeated identical lines have separate stable identities, including blank and CRLF lines
reason: Repeated text, blank lines and CRLF lines must retain separate stable IDs while redundant pushes emit nothing, preventing deduplication of intentional repeated speech.

test: permits unfinished-tail revisions but permanently invalidates revisions to committed speech
reason: Changing an unfinished tail is allowed, but changing an already-committed prefix must permanently invalidate the parser so delivered audio cannot be silently rewritten.

test: continue baselines preserve formatting context without emitting old complete lines
reason: Continue generation must retain old formatting context without emitting old complete lines, and report appended bytes/source positions for a previously unfinished line.

test: empty final response closes cleanly and continuation after a newline emits only new lines
reason: An empty final result must close cleanly; continuing from a newline-complete baseline must emit only new content at the correct source offset.

test: fences and hidden markup remain raw context for downstream host formatting and exclusions
reason: The line parser must retain raw fences/hidden markup as context rather than filtering them itself; downstream formatting owns exclusions, and the final visible tail still flushes correctly.

test: switching replies carries only the chosen reply plus later manual corrections
reason: Composes a second reply with later manual HP corrections while replacing inventory/time/memory effects, reconstructs the first reply and verifies input base remains unchanged. Protects pure rebase semantics.

test: a reply can add and remove collections while a manual profile edit survives
reason: Applies only a later profile appearance correction onto a different reply; old role and reply-owned memory do not leak. Retained for independent profile snapshot maps rather than tracker state.

test: actor edits follow names when another reply changes scene order
reason: Reorders actor arrays and applies a correction by actor name, verifying it reaches Ada rather than the old numeric index. Protects per-NPC identity.

test: manual scene removal survives a regenerated reply with the same message ID
reason: Rebases a regenerated same-ID reply after manual scene removal; verifies both actor absence and suppression persist. Covers deletion patches plus explicit presence state.

test: new scene actor does not fold an earlier manual correction into reply effects
reason: Adds a new actor after a prior manual HP correction; verifies reply-only effects do not adopt that correction and manual patch can still be reapplied. Protects snapshot attribution.

test: repeated swipe keeps each reply separate
reason: Repeats simple whole-value patch application for two HP alternatives; the broader reply/manual composition test already verifies these replacement semantics and real tracker swipe tests exercise state switching. Removed duplicate primitive case.
covered_by: tests/turn-delta.mjs — switching replies carries only the chosen reply plus later manual corrections; tests/tracker-swipe.mjs — a new swipe retaining outgoing prose restores the narrator base before generation

test: a saved effect for another swipe or edited text is rejected
reason: Checks effect identity requires both exact text and swipe and distinguishes absent/valid/mismatch. Protects source validation before replay.

test: new chat scope applies in the original chat
reason: Confirms category scope in unchanged chat invokes setChatCast; positive control ensures stale-result guard tests cannot pass because action never executes.

test: avatar alias picker returns the selected character
reason: Confirms alias picker returns the chosen card in unchanged chat; positive control for async ownership guard.

test: history cleanup cleans the original chat
reason: Confirms cleanup action invokes history cleaner in original chat; positive control for destructive action guard.

test: new chat scope ignores confirmation after chat switch
reason: Replaces chat metadata during scope popup and asserts no cast save; prevents delayed confirmation assigning categories to another chat.

test: avatar alias picker ignores confirmation after chat switch
reason: Replaces metadata during alias selection and expects null; prevents delayed alias choice linking a speaker in a different chat.

test: history cleanup ignores confirmation after chat switch
reason: Changes chat during cleanup confirmation and asserts cleaner never runs; protects another chat from destructive history cleanup.

test: bulk deletion keeps the selection named in its confirmation
reason: Changes selected IDs while bulk-delete confirmation is open and checks only originally confirmed item deletes; protects consent scope rather than incidental toolbar layout.

test: tracker display controls save and redraw without reprocessing chat
reason: Invokes every tracker display-setting change callback and asserts save/redraw without chat reprocessing; prevents changing display options from rerunning story reading or leaving stale tracker display.

test: linked lore entry with UID zero can generate and save
reason: Executes lore UI generation/save for linked UID zero, asserts correct world/UID/content/options/callback/close and a visible truncation warning; replaced token limit wording with nonempty warning check.

test: editor leaves an unavailable pictures view and its back button returns to the character list
reason: Changes available picture fields to none while editor retains pictures state, checks safe profile fallback and working Back callback; production permits this in-memory state after settings change, so not just legacy migration.

test: new character card opens its editor through the supplied callback
reason: Clicks new-card action, verifies trimmed name, chat inclusion and opening the resulting character through supplied editor callback; protects action wiring and avoids creating inaccessible cards.

test: starter picker imports and activates a fresh System before a chat starts
reason: Invokes the actual starter-button listener to import the selected factory definition with rule defaults, activate it and refresh theme/memory/chat UI. This detects broken action wiring that factory/import unit tests cannot; lookup text is a fixture selector, not an asserted label.

test: starter activation is disabled after a chat has selected its System
reason: Builds the manager for a started chat and verifies the starter activation control is disabled. This is a UI gate complementing the state-layer refusal to switch an owned chat; it does not prove browser interaction/rendering.

test: finalized streaming cues retain the identity used for their first synthesis
reason: Finalizing a streamed voice cue must reuse its provisional synthesis ID, save only the first assignment and preserve that identity across chat serialization; later cues cannot redesign an existing voice.

test: accepts only a complete first cue for a recognized NPC in the reply
reason: Cue parsing must accept only a completed line for a recognized non-player speaker, deduplicate repeats and reject unknown/cardless speaker sets; this prevents arbitrary voice assignments.

reason: Fenced cues, inline narration annotations, broken quoting and multiline values must not become voice designs, preventing hidden/code text and incomplete streaming metadata from being used.
